extracted.intended_audience: newsroom managers, journalists, digital preservationists, archivists, and news organization leadership
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preserving digitally distributed news content (web articles, interactives, social posts) within news organizations, including policy, technical, and workflow considerations. Aimed at establishing sustainable practices to capture a holistic record of what newsrooms publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic record preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations must save a holistic record of what they produce — not just article text — because a news product often consists of a headline, byline, text, images, comments, interactive features, embedded video, and outgoing links, plus curated links posted to third-party platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preservation plans should capture all constituent elements of a published story and related outputs (embedded media, interactives, comments, outbound links, and third-party social postings). Consider that content posted or promoted on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and other platforms is part of the published record and should be accounted for in archiving workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented archival policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Have formal, documented policies for the preservation of digital content rather than no policy or only informal/ad-hoc practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear written policies that define responsibilities, scope, retention, technical approaches, and review cycles. Avoid relying on undocumented or accidental practices; document procedures so preservation survives staff turnover and organizational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve social media publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media postings (tweets, Facebook posts, Instagram posts, etc.) that constitute part of a news organization's output must be preserved; interviewees reported none were preserving their social media publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include social media capture in archiving strategies and define mechanisms and frequencies for capturing posts, replies, threads, embeds, and metadata from third-party platforms. Address API limits, legal/terms-of-service issues, and linkages between social posts and published stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate backups/cloud storage with preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Backing up content on content management systems or cloud-based servers is not the same as preservation; many newsrooms confuse the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between operational backups (for disaster recovery) and long-term preservation (which requires format migration, metadata, integrity checks, and access planning). Design workflows and storage with preservation-grade controls (checksums, redundancy, documented formats), not just copies on cloud servers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive dynamic/interactive news applications and apps
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive and dynamic news applications are at high risk of being lost because their underlying technologies can become obsolete before they are saved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop strategies to capture and preserve interactive features and applications — e.g., through emulation, code preservation, containerization, or specialized capture tools. Engage newsroom developers in preservation planning and evaluate emulation-based web archiving tools under development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on the Internet Archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Many staff rely on the Internet Archive to preserve publications, but web archiving has limitations in the formats it can capture and preserves only a fraction of online publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Internet Archive as one resource but supplement with local, institutional, or partner-based archiving solutions that can capture additional formats and parts of the record. Assess what IA can/cannot capture and plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make archiving processes simple and workflow-friendly
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital archiving efforts succeed only if the process is simple in terms of implementation and day-to-day workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design low-friction tools and workflows that integrate with journalists’ and editors’ routines; automate capture where possible; provide clear, easy-to-follow steps so staff do not have to choose between publishing and preserving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build partnerships across archivists, technologists, memory institutions, and news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful preservation requires collaboration among archivists, technologists, memory institutions, and newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form partnerships to share expertise and services. Collaborative planning should start by answering: What should be preserved? Who should preserve it? Leverage partners for storage, technical expertise, and institutional longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define scope and capture frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide what to preserve and how often (e.g., how often to capture an ever-updating home page, whether to preserve personalized content and newsletters, and what to do with reader comments and social posts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish capture frequency policies (e.g., periodic snapshots, event-driven captures), rules for personalized or transient content, and clear choices on whether and how to preserve comments and newsletters. Balance thoroughness against cost and technical feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain management buy-in and identify opinion leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: To enact lasting change, it is key to find opinion leaders who can introduce archiving ideas and to convince management of archiving's advantages and compatibility with priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target managers and decision-makers with clear business cases, risk assessments, and demonstrations of low-friction solutions. Use respected practitioners and internal champions to model and advocate for archiving practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve both reporting documentation and published output
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists often preserve documentation of reporting (notes, evidence) but neglect preserving what ultimately gets published; both must be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include published outputs in preservation plans in addition to internal documentation. Ensure that the final published versions — including presentation, layout, embeds, and associated social promotion — are captured and linked to reporting archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for longevity and technological change
rubrics_metrics.description: Archival strategies should ensure current practices have the longevity to outlast changes in technology; ad-hoc approaches may fail as platforms and formats evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design preservation with format migration, emulation, documented file formats, and institutional commitments in mind. Create formal strategies that consider obsolescence, funding, and stewardship beyond current technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage existing archiving initiatives and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: There are existing initiatives and tools (e.g., PastPages, NewsGrabber, Archive-It) that news organizations can learn from or enlist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey and pilot established tools and community projects to avoid reinventing solutions. Evaluate third-party projects for fit with newsroom workflows, coverage of required formats, and long-term sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate resources and planning to archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: The industry needs to reassess priorities and address significant shortfalls in resources and planning for preservation if future access is to be assured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for preservation staffing, infrastructure, training, and partnerships. Treat archiving as a funded, planned activity rather than an optional or ad-hoc task; include it in strategic planning and risk management.
